audit: VERTEX Kattis candidate original-statement evidence ledger — pass 5

summary.sourceQualityNote: Boggle statement source is a mirror; treat provenance as lower confidence pending official contest archive confirmation.

method: Inspected original contest statements or contest statement copies for problem identity, narrative, input/output and constraints. These records do not establish current live Kattis page availability or long-scenario eligibility.

records.title: Train Passengers
records.identity: PDF explicitly gives problem ID trainpassengers and title Train Passengers
records.observed: Consultants audit station-master counts of people leaving, entering and waiting, and determine whether train capacity, nonnegative passenger counts and final-empty conditions remain consistent across stations.
records.excerpt: The Nordic Company of Passing Carriages is losing money at an alarming rate because most of their trains are empty.
records.inputOutput: Input: train capacity, station count, and per-station leaving/entering/waiting counts. Output: possible or impossible.
records.constraints: 2 ≤ n ≤ 100 stations; all values including capacity are between 0 and 10^9.
records.scenarioNotes: Strong operational narrative and sequential consistency checks, but a single-pass simulation. Long-scenario depth not approved.

records.title: Financial Planning
records.identity: PDF explicitly gives Problem F Financial Planning and matches the Kattis problem title
records.observed: A young adult needs a retirement target and can borrow arbitrary principal interest-free, investing once in each opportunity; each investment has an initial cost and daily profit, and the goal is minimum time until investments can be repaid and the target retained.
records.excerpt: You are currently broke, but fortunately a generous gazillionaire friend has offered to lend you an arbitrary amount of money
records.inputOutput: Input: number of investments and required retirement amount, then each investment's daily profit and initial cost. Output: minimum days to repay principal and retain at least the target.
records.constraints: 1 ≤ n ≤ 100,000; 1 ≤ M ≤ 10^9; each daily profit and initial cost between 1 and 10^9.
records.scenarioNotes: Realistic financial planning narrative with a clear investment decision model and scale constraints; promising contextual candidate, but one optimization task only. Long-scenario qualification remains pending.

records.title: Boggle
records.identity: Problem set lists A Boggle; Kattis ICPC archive maps Boggle to slug boggle and Germany 2013
records.observed: The statement describes the 4×4 Boggle board game, adjacency in eight directions, no reusing a die within a word, dictionary validation and scoring by word length.
records.excerpt: A Boggle is a 4 × 4 grid of letters where your job is to find as many words as you can.
records.inputOutput: Input: dictionary, then multiple 4×4 boards. Output: maximum score, longest word and number of distinct valid words per board.
records.constraints: Dictionary has 1 < w < 300,000 words, each up to 8 uppercase letters; 1 < b < 30 boards.
records.scenarioNotes: Detailed game rules and multi-part scoring/output, but still a compact search problem. Statement source is a mirror rather than an official contest host; source provenance is weaker than other rows.

records.title: Sudoku
records.identity: KTH-hosted original NWERC PDF lists Problem A Sudoku and its full statement; archive metadata maps sudoku to NWERC 2006
records.observed: Bill discovers that this week's Sudoku puzzle may be derived from last week's solved puzzle through rotations, row/column swaps within bands/stacks, band/stack swaps and digit permutations.
records.excerpt: Bill just realized that the sudoku puzzle he had spent the last ten minutes trying to solve essentially was last week’s puzzle, only rotated counterclockwise.
records.inputOutput: Input: prior solved Sudoku and current unsolved puzzle. Output Yes if the current puzzle can be derived using allowed transformations, otherwise No.
records.constraints: 0 ≤ N ≤ 50 test cases; each board is 9×9; uniqueness of each unsolved puzzle and validity of prior solutions are guaranteed.
records.scenarioNotes: Rich and explicit transformation story with several operation classes and a clear verification task. More scenario depth than a trivial Sudoku solver, but remains a finite transformation-validation problem. Candidate for human depth review, not auto-approved.
